title: Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) blocking PowerToys.PowerLauncher for Microsoft.Edit

judgment.rationale: The supplied event identifies Defender ASR Event 1121, rule GUID C0033C00-D16D-4114-A5A0-DC9B3A7D2CEB, an Entra-joined Intune-managed device, and a block while launching Microsoft Edit from PowerLauncher. Enforcement is an organization-managed Defender policy, not a PowerToys setting; the appropriate owner is the endpoint-security administrator.
evidence: Event ID 1121 and ASR rule GUID are provided.
Target is Microsoft Edit; parent process is PowerToys.PowerLauncher.exe.
judgment.recommended_action: Have the endpoint-security administrator review the named ASR rule and decide whether the signed PowerToys/Edit launch path should be allowed; do not weaken policy from PowerToys.

fix_assessment.rationale: PowerToys cannot override an organization-managed Defender ASR decision. The report gives the rule and process details needed for the policy owner; no PowerToys code fix is grounded.

issue_context.summary: Defender ASR blocks a Microsoft Edit launch originating from PowerToys.PowerLauncher on an Intune-managed device.
known_information: Author provides Event ID 1121, ASR rule GUID, process path, target Edit executable, and parent command line.
Author says the rule was configured earlier and began triggering after updating Microsoft Edit.
Device is Entra joined and managed through Intune.
inferences: The trigger may be the changed Microsoft Edit child process rather than a PowerToys defect.
Only the organization can decide whether to allow this execution under its ASR configuration.
issue_context.analysis: Route the event to the policy owner with the exact rule GUID and process chain; do not request duplicate diagnostics.
initial_investigation: Read complete issue body and attached report reference.
The event attributes the block to an IT-admin-configured Defender ASR rule and includes identifying details.
